title: 02. Data Structures: Data Structures — Advanced
summary: This comprehensive guide covers Python's core data structures with advanced concepts, performance optimization, and real-world applications.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: This comprehensive guide covers Python's core data structures with advanced concepts, performance optimization, and real-world applications.

sections.title: What's Covered
sections.body:
### Core Data Structures
- **Lists**: Advanced operations, memory management, performance optimization
- **Tuples**: Immutability benefits, unpacking techniques, use cases
- **Sets**: Mathematical operations, hash table internals, algorithms
- **Dictionaries**: Hash collision handling, optimization, advanced patterns

### Advanced Topics
- Memory management and garbage collection
- Data structure internals and implementation details
- Performance profiling and optimization techniques
- Thread-safe and concurrent data structures
- Algorithm implementations using data structures

sections.title: Getting Started
sections.body:
### Prerequisites
- Basic Python knowledge
- Understanding of object-oriented programming
- Familiarity with algorithm concepts

### Running the Examples
```bash
# Navigate to the data structures directory
cd topics/05_data_structures

# Run the comprehensive examples
python data_structures_examples.py

# Practice with exercises
python exercises.py
```

sections.title: Content Overview
sections.body:
### 1. Lists - Advanced Mutable Sequences
- **Creation Methods**: Range lists, matrix initialization, memory-efficient creation
- **Advanced Indexing**: Negative indexing, step slicing, nested access
- **Memory Optimization**: Growth strategy analysis, append vs concatenation
- **Performance Analysis**: Time complexity of operations, memory usage patterns
- **Advanced Comprehensions**: Nested loops, conditional filtering, complex transformations

### 2. Tuples - Advanced Immutable Sequences
- **Memory Efficiency**: Memory comparison with lists, hash table usage
- **Advanced Unpacking**: Extended unpacking with *, nested unpacking
- **Use Cases**: Configuration storage, coordinate systems, return values
- **Performance Benefits**: Creation speed, access time, iteration efficiency
- **Immutability Patterns**: Thread safety, hashable objects

### 3. Sets - Advanced Unordered Collections
- **Mathematical Operations**: Union, intersection, difference, symmetric difference
- **Frozensets**: Immutable sets, nested set operations
- **Performance Characteristics**: O(1) membership testing, hash table internals
- **Real-World Applications**: Data deduplication, permission systems, graph algorithms
- **Set-Based Algorithms**: Bloom filters, connected components, duplicate detection

### 4. Dictionaries - Advanced Key-Value Mappings
- **Hash Table Internals**: Collision handling, load factor management
- **Performance Optimization**: Memory usage, access patterns
- **Advanced Patterns**: Nested dictionaries, configuration management
- **Custom Hash Classes**: Hash collision demonstration, equality implementation

sections.body:

sections.title: Performance Analysis
sections.body:
### Memory Usage Comparison
```python
List:   ~72 bytes base + 8 bytes per element
Tuple:  ~56 bytes base + 8 bytes per element
Set:    ~736 bytes base + variable overhead
Dict:   ~296 bytes base + variable overhead
```

### Time Complexity
| Operation | List | Tuple | Set | Dict |
|-----------|------|-------|-----|------|
| Access    | O(1) | O(1)  | O(1)| O(1) |
| Search    | O(n) | O(n)  | O(1)| O(1) |
| Insert    | O(1) | N/A   | O(1)| O(1) |
| Delete    | O(n) | N/A   | O(1)| O(1) |

sections.title: Best Practices
sections.body:
### Memory Efficiency
1. Use generators for large datasets
2. Prefer tuples for immutable data
3. Use `__slots__` for classes with many instances
4. Consider frozensets for immutable collections

### Performance Optimization
1. Choose appropriate data structures for use cases
2. Profile before optimizing
3. Use built-in functions and methods
4. Avoid premature optimization

### Code Quality
1. Use type hints for better documentation
2. Implement proper error handling
3. Write comprehensive tests
4. Document performance characteristics
